info.name: AISafe - Maintenance Service (WP#4, Assignment 2: CQRS + AMQP)
info.description: Maintenance with 3 replicas (8082/8182/8282), RabbitMQ, Aircraft Management (8081/8181/8281) and Flight Routes. Start everything with scripts/start-all.* (demo profile recommended). Run folders 0-7 in order; stop maintenance-2 before folder 8 and start it again before folder 9. The databases are files (code/data/), so the collection can be run again: template names carry a run id.

item.name: 0 - Setup (tokens, run id)
item.description: Run first. Stores the tokens, today's date and a run id (template names are unique per run, because the databases are files and survive restarts).

item.name: 1 - CQRS: template written on one replica, read on all
item.description: The command (POST) runs on replica 2 and publishes MaintenanceTemplateCreated to RabbitMQ (exchange aisafe.maintenance.events). Replicas 1 and 3 project it into their own read model REPLICATED_MAINTENANCE_TEMPLATE and answer the GETs locally.

pm.test('no duplicated ids', () => pm.expect(new Set(b.map(t => t.id)).size).to.eql(b.length));

2 - Records and the asynchronous integration with Aircraft Management
item.description: US115. The record is written on the replica that receives the POST (its owner). Aircraft Management is told synchronously (B3b PATCH, a command with an immediate answer); its AircraftStatusChanged event then reaches every consumer: Maintenance's KNOWN_AIRCRAFT and Aircraft Management's AIRCRAFT_MOOD (/api/v2/unicorns).

exec: pm.test('IN_PROGRESS, checklist of the template, owner replica 2', () => { pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('IN_PROGRESS'); pm.expect(b.checklist.length).to.eql(4); pm.expect(b.ownerInstance).to.eql('maintenance-2'); });
setTimeout(() => {}, 1500); // eventual consistency: give the event time to reach the other replicas

item.name: Aircraft Management read model /api/v2/unicorns: CS-TUA is GROUNDED_AND_GRUMPY

exec: pm.test('mood updated by the AircraftStatusChanged event', () => { pm.expect(a.operationalStatus).to.eql('UNDER_MAINTENANCE'); pm.expect(a.mood).to.eql('GROUNDED_AND_GRUMPY'); pm.expect(a.source).to.eql('read-model'); });

3 - Queries answered by any replica from its read model
item.description: Every GET reads only the local read model REPLICATED_MAINTENANCE_RECORD (no peer call, no X-Partial-Response). ownerInstance tells which replica owns (writes) the record.

4 - Commands executed by the owner replica
item.description: A PATCH that reaches a replica that does not own the record is forwarded (HTTP, X-Service-Key) to the owner, which changes its write model and publishes the event. When the last ongoing record of an aircraft is completed, the aircraft is released (B3b) and the AircraftStatusChanged event updates the moods.

item.name: 5 - Statistics, reports and alerts (read models)
item.description: Computed by any replica from its own read models: the records of every replica (REPLICATED_MAINTENANCE_RECORD), the fleet (KNOWN_AIRCRAFT, Aircraft Management events) and the flight minutes (KNOWN_SCHEDULED_FLIGHT, Flight Routes events).

item.name: US117 maintenance hours of the fleet
US221 average turnaround per model (same on every replica)

exec: pm.test('average = total minutes / completed records', () => pm.expect(a320.averageMinutes).to.be.closeTo(a320.totalMinutes / a320.completedRecords, 0.01));

pm.test('alerts have aircraft, template and trigger', () => b.forEach(a => { pm.expect(a.aircraftRegistration).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(['FLIGHT_HOURS','CALENDAR_DAYS']).to.include(a.trigger); }));
pm.test('no alert for inactive aircraft (CS-TUF)', () => pm.expect(b.map(a => a.aircraftRegistration)).to.not.include('CS-TUF'));

item.name: 7 - /api/v2/unicorns mock (CQRS read-model contract)
item.description: Mandatory mock of the assignment. Set unicornsMockUrl to your Postman mock server (create it from this collection or from 'AISafe - Unicorns Mock': docs/2-containers/Unicorns-Mock.md). It is a pure query: the same contract is served for real by Aircraft Management's AIRCRAFT_MOOD read model (folders 2 and 4), which is fed by the AircraftStatusChanged events that Maintenance causes when a record starts or ends.

request.description: Query only. Each item is one aircraft as known by the read model (registration, model, operational status), plus the derived mood, the time of the last status event applied and source = "read-model".

item.name: 8 - Replica failure (STOP maintenance-2 first)
item.description: Close the window of maintenance-2 before running this folder. Its records stay readable on the other replicas (read model) - in Assignment 1 they gave 404. Commands on its records need the owner: 503. New records are written by the replicas that are up.

item.name: Record owned by replica 2 is still readable on replica 1 (200, read model)

exec: pm.test('same report as before the failure', () => pm.expect(JSON.stringify(pm.response.json())).to.eql(pm.environment.get('turnaroundOnM1')));

item.name: Command on a record of replica 2 -> 503 (owner down)
New record on replica 1 while replica 2 is down
9 - Replica 2 is back (START maintenance-2 again first)
item.description: Start maintenance-2 again and wait until it is UP. The events published while it was down waited in its durable queue maintenance-2.maintenance and are applied when it reconnects.

item.name: Replica 2 caught up: it has the record created while it was down

exec: setTimeout(() => {}, 1500); // eventual consistency: give the event time to reach the other replicas
pm.test('COMPLETED, owned by replica 1', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('COMPLETED'); pm.expect(b.ownerInstance).to.eql('maintenance-1'); });
